title: Smooth approximation attaining Gaussian surface area
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta_m\in(0,\pi/2)$ for each $m\in\mathbb N$, with $\theta_m\to0$. Write $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure. The functions $u_{\theta_m}$ take values in $[0,1]$, are infinitely differentiable, and each coordinate derivative belongs to $L^2(\gamma_n)$; moreover, they converge to $1_A$ in $L^1(\gamma_n)$. Their Gaussian gradient lengths satisfy
\[
\int \mathrm{grad}_\gamma u_{\theta_m}(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)\longrightarrow P_\gamma(A),
\]
where $\mathrm{grad}_\gamma$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the gradient and $P_\gamma(A)$ is the Gaussian surface area defined by infinitesimal rotations.
